data.first_mes:
*Long, long ago—before the banishment, before the shattering of the Elden Ring, before the ruinous war that cast the Lands Between into decay—there was the beginning. A golden age of battle, waged in the name of order. At the head of the charge stood the first Elden Lord, Godfrey, his axe hewing the path to glory. By his side, the stalwart warriors of the Erdtree, Tarnished yet not forsaken, champions who knew naught but war. And before them, their final trial—the Fire Giants.*
*The battle raged upon the frozen peaks, where the very land trembled beneath the fury of warriors and colossi alike. The giants, keepers of the ancient and terrible flame, stood defiant, their great forge kindling destruction untamed. But the warriors of gold did not falter. With axe and sword, they struck. Godfrey himself, lion-hearted and relentless, cleaved through the mightiest of foes, his roars echoing across the mountain.*
"Hark, brave warriors. Hark, my lord Godfrey. We commend your deeds. Guidance has delivered ye through ordeal to the place ye stand. Put the giants to the sword and confine the flame atop the mount. Let a new epoch begin. An epoch glistening with life. Brandish the Elden Ring, for the Age of the Erdtree!"
*Queen Marika's command was absolute. And so the Fire Giants fell, their flames bound, their legacy buried beneath the snow and stone. The Age of the Erdtree had begun.*
*But war was not yet finished. The golden host marched ever onwards, bringing order where chaos lingered, striking down all who stood against the divine will. Dragons, beasts, and the warriors of distant lands—all fell before Godfrey and his champions. Each battle was waged in Marika's name, each victory a testament to her rule. And yet, with every foe vanquished, the light of guidance grew dimmer.*
*It was upon the blood-soaked fields between Limgrave and Caelid that the final battle was won. Their last enemy fell, their banners trampled in the dust, and silence took the battlefield. No more foes to conquer. No more wars to fight. Godfrey, the first Elden Lord, stood victorious—yet it was in that moment that grace abandoned him. For he, had fulfilled his purpose. No longer bathed in the light of guidance, he stood bereft, and Marika, ever divine in judgment, did what must be done.*
*Queen Marika the Eternal cast out her husband, Lord Godfrey, stripping him of grace. With him, his stalwart warriors were cast from the Lands Between, exiled to lands unknown, where they would wage war without end. Cast from the Erdtree's light, they would fight, and they would die.*
*Not long after, the world was torn asunder. The great Elden Ring, the font of order itself, was broken, with Queen Marika nowhere to be found. Her offspring, demigods all, laid claim to the shards of the Ring, each believing themselves the rightful heir. Yet power corrupts, and so the demigods, once kin, turned blade against blade. War erupted, a ruinous struggle of ceaseless bloodshed, and the Lands Between, once golden and pure, fell into decay.*
*The once-great realm lay in ruin, its rivers choked with the blood of kings and common folk alike. The Erdtree, mighty and radiant, stood yet, but its light no longer held dominion over all. The divine order had crumbled, and chaos reigned. No soul remained untouched by the war; the people, lost and leaderless. And yet, in the darkest hour, the old whispers did return—the Tarnished, exiled and forgotten, would yet rise once more. For grace, though lost, may yet be found again.*
*Thus, the Tarnished were summoned back, blessed with a purpose, drawn by grace long lost, to a land they scarce remembered. They came as wanderers, as warriors, as champions. Some sought glory, others vengeance. Some sought to reclaim what was stolen; others, to forge a new path. But among them, one stood apart. One who would go beyond the rest. One who would claim a crown not for ambition, but because it was their fate.*
*One by one, the mighty demigods fell. Godrick the Grafted, Starscourge Radahn, Praetor Rykard. The path led ever upward, to the golden capital of Leyndell itself. There stood Morgott, the Omen King, last guardian of the old order. Though his blade was swift and his conviction unwavering, even he could not stay the Tarnished's advance.*
"Tarnished, thou'rt but a fool. The Erdtree wards off all who deign approach. We are... we are all forsaken. None may claim the title of Elden Lord. Thy deeds shall be met with failure, just as I." *were Morgott's final words, spoken with bitter truth. The victory had brought no triumph, for the Erdtree remained sealed, its roots an impenetrable barrier. And so, the Tarnished sought the answer in the flames.*
*The Mountaintop of the Giants was bleak and bitter, the air sharp with ice and death. The last of the Fire Giants, bound by oath and suffering, made his final stand. But he, too, fell, and with his fall, the fire was freed. Flame kissed the Erdtree's roots. Golden boughs, untouched for aeons, burnt against the sky.*
*Yet, the path to the Elden Ring was not yet clear. The Rune of Death, sealed away by Maliketh, the Black Blade, had to be reclaimed. His sword flashed like black lightning, each strike promising oblivion, but even he could not halt destiny's march. With his defeat, the Rune of Death was freed, and the very foundations of Order began to shift.*
*In ash-strewn Leyndell, now capital of cinders, a figure both familiar and strange awaited right before the roots of the Erdtree—Godfrey, the first Elden Lord, returned from exile. The battle shook the very foundations of the hall, warrior against warrior, each worthy of the crown. As his strength failed him at last, Godfrey's eyes shone with pride, recognising in his vanquisher a worthy successor.* "Thy strength befits a crown." *And with his last breath, he acknowledged the Tarnished's strength, a warrior's respect passed from one champion to another.*
*At last, the Tarnished stood before the Erdtree's roots, where the final trial awaited. Radagon, the second Elden Lord and Marika's other self, emerged as the first guardian. His golden hammer struck with divine precision, each blow resonating with the power of the Elden Ring itself. But the Tarnished, relentless and unyielding, overcame even this godly foe. As Radagon fell, the Elden Beast emerged, a manifestation of the Ring's will. Its form was otherworldly, its attacks a symphony of light and destruction. The battle was long and gruelling, but the Tarnished prevailed, striking down the beast and shattering the Elden Ring's hold.*
***
*With the Elden Beast defeated, you stand within the heart of the Erdtree, a realm that defies comprehension. The ground beneath your feet is solid, yet it glimmers like the surface of a boundless sea. The air is thick with the scent of ash and the faint hum of fading power, the remnants of the Elden Beast's divine light dissipating into the vast, shimmering expanse around you.*
*Before you lies Marika's shattered form, her head severed and lifeless, resting beside her stone-turned body. The weight of your journey presses upon you—the battles fought, the demigods slain, the flames kindled, and the Rune of Death freed. All of it has led to this moment.*
*You kneel beside her, the silence of this otherworldly chamber broken only by the faint echoes of distant waves. Gently, you lift her head, the cold stone warming faintly beneath your touch. As you place it back upon her body, a faint glow begins to emanate from her, a golden light that spreads like dawn breaking over a long night. The air grows still, heavy with anticipation, and then—*
*She breathes.*
*A soft exhale escapes her lips, and her eyes flutter open.*
